title: The radio-infrared nebula in II Zw 40: clusters forming in colliding elongated clouds
question: Deduce the history of the current active starburst centered on the radio-infrared supernebula in II Zw 40 and test whether it is the collision or merger of two star clusters associated with elongated molecular clouds.

what.value: Luminosity and mass of SSC-N (9.1 +/- 1 x 10^5 M_sun, 1.1 +/- 0.1 x 10^9 L_sun)

evidence.quote: The luminosity and mass of SSC-N deduced from optical and UV observations are an order of magnitude greater than those of 30 Doradus (9 . 1±1×10 [5] M ⊙, 1 . 1±0 . 1×10 [9] L ⊙, (Leitherer et al. 2018)).

what.value: Molecular gas mass on components W and C (3.5 x 10^5 M_sun) and source positions/identifications (W, C, E)

evidence.loc: 3.2 Spatial Structure of Dense Molecular Gas
evidence.quote: The dominant molecular peak marked as ’W4’ in Figure 6, agrees with Consiglio et al. (2017)’s CO and 3 mm continuum peak ’W’, and is co-incident with the radio and infrared cluster.
the 3.5×10 [5] M ⊙ of molecular gas Consiglio et al. (2017) find on ’W’ and ’C’ is less than the stellar mass deduced for the clusters.

what.value: Upper range of the age of SSC-N (3 Myr)

evidence.quote: As the upper range of the age of SSC-N is 3Myr Vanzi et al. (2008), both options are at present valid and the simulations cannot at present distinguish.

recipe.goal: Map radio continuum and mid-IR [S IV] emission of ionized gas
recipe.method: Clean and image JVLA 15 and 22 GHz continuum data with natural and Briggs (robust = 0) weighting; scan Gemini North TEXES slit across target to build [S IV] 10.5 um spectral cube; collapse cube and extract spectrum and 2-Gaussian fit.
key_parameters: robust = 0 (Briggs weighting) and natural weighting for JVLA maps
TEXES cube: 23 x 0.25 arcsec pixels in RA, 32 x 0.14 arcsec pixels in Dec, 256 x 0.95 km s^-1 channels
assumptions: T_e ~ 10^4 K giving S^+++ thermal broadening of ~3.5 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Analyze spatial distribution and kinematics of CO(3-2) molecular gas
recipe.method: Generate moment 0, 1, and 2 maps, position-velocity diagrams (PVDs) along RA and Dec, and region-integrated line profiles (5 positions) from the continuum-subtracted ALMA CO(3-2) spectral cube.
key_parameters: 2 km s^-1 spectral channels, 0.34 x 0.25 arcsec beam

recipe.goal: Simulate individual star cluster evolution prior to collision
recipe.method: Evolve two isolated star clusters (large and small) for 2 Myr using AMUSE coupling N-body (ph4), Tree-SPH (GADGET-2), stellar evolution (SeBA), and stellar winds ('heat' mode) via a Bridge scheme.
key_parameters: Cluster total masses: 4.5 x 10^5 M_sun (large) and 2.2 x 10^5 M_sun (small); O star counts: 4300 and 2150
SPH particle mass = 1.5 M_sun; initial gas T = 10^4 K; evolution time = 2 Myr; timestep = 10 kyr
assumptions: Star cluster has already formed in each clump prior to collision; gas comprises 70% of total cluster mass
Plummer sphere for gas; King model for stars; Salpeter IMF in mass range [15, 120] M_sun

recipe.goal: Simulate cluster-cluster collisions and generate synthetic CO(3-2) and [S IV] observations
recipe.method: Trim evolved clusters to slightly above virial radius, collide them over a grid of impact parameters (b = 0 to 6 pc), interpolate SPH gas properties onto a 3D grid, run RADMC-3D at inclinations of 45, 60, and 75 deg, convolve with observed beam, and compare moment 0, PVDs, and line profiles to ALMA and TEXES observations.
key_parameters: Initial collision velocity ~ 120 km s^-1; impact parameter b = 0 to 6 pc in 0.5 pc increments; runtime = 0.5 Myr with 10^4 yr timestep
RADMC-3D grid: 256 x 256 x 256 covering 60 x 60 x 60 pc; inclinations: 45, 60, and 75 deg
assumptions: Large-scale spatial distribution and kinematics of CO and [S IV] are similar as they roughly trace the same gas mass

score_reason: Raw observational datasets (ALMA, JVLA, Gemini) are public and basic observational metrics (flux, size, line velocities) can be re-measured from the cubes/maps, but ALMA imaging parameters are largely omitted (likely inherited from Consiglio et al. 2016/2017) and the AMUSE/RADMC-3D simulation scripts and several initial condition / radiative transfer parameters are not released.
rediscovery_reason: All observational data (ALMA 2013.1.00122.S, JVLA 16B-067, Gemini GN-2017A-Q-57) are public in observatory archives, and the primary observational measurements (22 GHz clump size and flux, [S IV] and CO(3-2) velocity components and PVDs) can be directly reproduced from the archival data.
